newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish MP quits party ahead of key Yilmaz vote.
newsitem.headline: Turkish MP quits party ahead of key Yilmaz vote.

text.p: A Turkish MP resigned from the opposition True Path Party on Friday, boosting Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz a day ahead of a confidence vote in the new anti-Islamist government.
Anatolian news agency said deputy Demir Berberoglu, head of parliament's human rights committee, had quit the conservative party.

Yilmaz, head of a rival right-wing party, has around a dozen more deputies on paper than he needs to win the vote in the 550-seat assembly. It was not immediately clear whether Berberoglu would support the government in Saturday's vote.
A key leftist party with 49 deputies pledged support for the left-right coalition at a debate on the government programme on Thursday.
Islamist former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned last month after a long, bitter row with the secularist military over religious activism.
The new government has said it will hold early elections next year, well before polls are due in the year 2000.
